title: WPSS/1166/2019 of VINOTRI KHATI Vs SUPERINTENDENT OF POLICE UTTARKASHI

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1166 of 2019
Vinotri Khati Ö Petitioner
Vs
Superintendent of Police & others Ö Respondents
Mr. Ayush Negi, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. Sushil Vashisth, learned Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.
Ms. Beena Pande, Additional C.S.C. for the State of Uttar Pradesh.
Honíble Manoj K. Tiwari, J. (Oral)
1. Petitioner was appointed as Constable in Uttar
Pradesh Police in the year 1986. She was transferred from
Muzaffarnagar to Uttarakshi vide order dated 22.07.1992.
Petitioner tendered her resignation vide letter dated
01.10.1992. Since petitioner did not join at the transferred
place, therefore a charge-sheet was issued to her on
28.08.1993. Against the said charge-sheet, petitioner filed
Writ Petition No. 3622 of 1994 before Allahabad High Court
and by an order dated 02.02.1994, the disciplinary enquiry
was stayed. The said writ petition was dismissed for want of
prosecution vide order dated 14.05.2012.
2. Now, petitioner has filed this writ petition seeking
following reliefs:-
(i) Issue a writ of order or direction in the nature of
certiorari quashing the entire departmental
proceedings against the petitioner being belated in
nature.
(ii) Issue a writ or order or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing the respondents to decide the
period of employment of the petitioner in view of non
acceptance of her resignation letter dated 1.10.1992
and further clear her pending salary dues.
(iii) Issue a writ order or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing the respondent authorities to
pay the entire salary during the period of
departmental enquiry and other service benefits.
3. Since petitioner had earlier filed writ petition,
challenging the disciplinary enquiry before Honíble Allahabad
High Court, which petition has been dismissed, therefore,
petitioner cannot file second writ petition for the same cause of

2
action. In such view of the matter, first prayer cannot be
granted to the petitioner.
4. Second and third prayers also cannot be granted to
the petitioner, as petitioner has slept over her rights for more
than 25 years. Moreover, she cannot get any monetary benefit
for this period, while she had not served.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner then submits that
petitioner is entitled to get G.P.F. and other monetary benefits,
therefore, petitioner may be permitted to make representation
and the Competent Authority may be asked to take decision
thereupon.
6. Prayer made is innocuous, therefore, is worth
accepting.
7. Accordingly, writ petition is disposed of with liberty
to the petitioner to make representation, claiming monetary
benefit, if any, to the Competent Authority, within three weeks
from today. If such representation is made, the Competent
Authority shall examine the claim of the petitioner and take
appropriate decision, in accordance with law, within three
months from the date of production of such representation
along with certified copy of this order.
 (Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
27. 5.2019 0
